title: A GUI input queued on gui_lock across a human handback executes with no open burst, so its changes get no snapshot and no gui_changes row
description: AgentBox decides whether a GUI input needs a snapshot before it acquires gui_lock. While a human holds the desktop a takeover lease exists, so GuiBursts.needs_snapshot returns False and the input blocks on gui_lock instead of opening a burst. If the human hands the desktop back while that input is queued, the input runs with a lease check that now passes and no burst open: it writes as uid 1001, calls mark_input, and its fresh input timestamp makes needs_snapshot False for every later input until 60 s of input silence (gui_snapshot_idle) or 600 s after the last snapshot (gui_snapshot_interval). Those inputs produce no snapshot, no burst, and no gui_changes row; the only recovery point predates the human takeover, and the file effects of the inputs are never diffed or attributed.
root_cause: The burst decision is taken outside the lock that serializes execution: service.py:343 evaluates _needs_snapshot (gui_bursts.py:52-63, which returns False while a non-stale lease or pending takeover exists) before _run_tool acquires gui_lock at service.py:136, and the only re-check under the lock (_check_control, service.py:152-161) validates the stale-lease/lease/pending-takeover state, never burst presence. _handback_locked (service.py:528-543) releases the lease (542) and calls forget_input (543) while still holding gui_lock, so the queued input resumes into a state where its earlier premise is gone and nothing takes a snapshot; mark_input (service.py:139) then suppresses the next burst decision.
intended_behavior: Every GUI input that executes must be covered by an open burst bound to a snapshot taken before that input, and each burst must close into a gui_changes record (service.py:261-264 fails closed when a burst baseline cannot be opened; gui_bursts.py:157-162 re-timers lifecycle paths for exactly this reason). A burst decision taken before waiting on a lock must be re-validated after the lock is acquired.

trace.description: Agent token from principal; default_policy.yaml has default: allow and no rule for click/type/key, so GUI inputs are approval-free, are audited as tool_request, and take the ALLOW branch.

_needs_snapshot is evaluated before any lock; while a takeover lease is present _over_snapshot_quota is skipped too and GuiBursts.needs_snapshot returns False, so no snapshot is taken and no burst is opened.
gui_lock is acquired afterwards without a timeout, so an input that already decided 'no burst needed' can sit queued while the human's handback holds the same lock.
The only re-check after acquiring gui_lock handles a stale lease, a live lease and the pending-takeover marker; burst presence and the earlier needs_snapshot result are never re-validated.
While gui_lock is still held, the human handback releases the lease; the queued input then acquires the lock with no lease and no pending marker, so _check_control passes.
forget_input only drops the input timestamp; the handback opens no burst, so the resumed input's decision premise is gone but nothing forces a snapshot.
The resumed input executes the GUI action and calls bursts.mark_input although no burst is open.
The fresh input timestamp makes the next decision False, so later inputs run burstless until gui_snapshot_idle of silence or gui_snapshot_interval since the last snapshot.
Only an open burst is ever diffed and logged as gui_changes; no burst exists for these inputs, so their /workspace changes are never recorded.

evidence.description: Burst decision taken before the lock; with a lease present it is False.
gui_lock is acquired after that decision, with no timeout.
_check_control re-checks only stale lease, lease and pending takeover; no burst-presence condition.
The handback releases the lease inside the gui_lock-held section.
forget_input in the same section clears the timestamp but opens no burst.
needs_snapshot returns False while a non-stale lease or pending takeover exists, assuming the input will get 423.
mark_input runs for an input that has no burst open.
A fresh input timestamp suppresses the following burst decision.
No burst, so no gui_changes row for the changes made by these inputs.
_snap_locks serializes SNAPSHOT_TOOLS, so at most one GUI input per sandbox is in _call_tool at a time; the window is the handback's lock-held section, not a queue of many inputs.
gui_snapshot_idle default 60 s: the burstless window ends after that much input silence.
gui_snapshot_interval default 600 s: upper bound with continuous input, because a snapshot older than that forces a new burst.

conditions.description: A sandbox agent token (agt_...); GUI tools are default-allow (default_policy.yaml default: allow) and need no human approval.

The single in-flight GUI input must take its burst decision while the takeover lease exists and then acquire gui_lock after the handback released the lease. A tight loop of click/type calls during the takeover (each 423) raises the hit rate; the window is the handback's lock-held section (audit write plus lease release), which SQLite/audit contention widens.
The human must hand the desktop back through handback, logout, or pause/restore/delete via end_desktop, because that path is the one that holds gui_lock across the lease release.

A snapshot taken within gui_snapshot_interval (default 600 s) exists, so after the burstless input the fresh mark_input timestamp keeps later inputs from opening a burst; the queued input itself needs only the lease.

execution.attacker_perspective: An agent that wants to change the desktop without a gui_changes row and without a fresh recovery point keeps issuing GUI inputs while a human holds the desktop, so one of them is queued on gui_lock when the human hands back, and then keeps clicking/typing immediately afterwards.
payloads: POST /sandboxes/sb_x/tools/click {"args":{"x":1,"y":1}} (opens the first burst and snapshot)
repeated POST /sandboxes/sb_x/tools/click {"args":{"x":2,"y":2}} while a takeover lease is held; all but the one landing in the handback window return 423
POST /sandboxes/sb_x/tools/click and /tools/type immediately after the handback
instructions: Bounded harness in the approved audit sandbox (sbx.py v08, no network, /target read-only): real AgentBox, GuiBursts and DesktopControl (sqlite :memory:); fake SandboxManager (click/type add a manifest entry), in-memory AuditLog with one hook, default-allow Policy, empty ApprovalStore.
Seed one click so a snapshot (snap_1) and an open burst exist; call box.takeover(sid, 'hs_human') so the burst is closed and a lease is held.

Install a hook on AuditLog.append('human_handback'): it starts the agent's click thread, waits until that thread has recorded its needs_snapshot decision (False, lease present, no burst), verifies it is blocked on gui_lock, then returns so box.handback(sid, 'hs_human') can release the lease and unlock.
Join the agent thread, then issue three more clicks, and read snapshot count, bursts._gui_burst, audit gui_changes rows and needs_snapshot.
Control run on a fresh box: seed click, three clicks while the burst is open, then takeover to close the burst, and compare the gui_changes diff.
execution.observed_result: The queued click executed with status 200 executed and needs_snapshot False taken while the lease was still present and no burst open; snapshots stayed 1 and gui_changes stayed at the single row the takeover wrote for the seed burst, while the click plus three following clicks (all 200) added 4 files (5 files total). All four burst decisions were False, so no new snapshot or burst appeared. The control run with the same four clicks inside an open burst logged gui_changes added=4 for snap_1 when the burst closed. The only artificial element is a pause inside the handback's audit append (a real SQLite write), which widens the natural window; the ordering it produces is one the code allows.

remediation.strategy: Decide the GUI burst requirement under the same lock that serializes GUI execution: after gui_lock is acquired in _run_tool, re-evaluate needs_snapshot and take the snapshot / open the burst there, and fail closed with reset_timers if no burst is open. Key the decision on burst presence rather than only on input timestamps, and make the handback path force the next input to open a new burst instead of only forgetting the timestamp. Regression test: hold gui_lock with an input queued, release the lease inside the lock, release the lock, and assert the input never calls mark_input or executes without an open burst.

code_changes.fixed_code:
def is_open(self, sid: str) -> bool:
    """입력이 실행될 때 열린 구간이 있는가. 구간 없이 실행하면 바뀐 것이 기록되지 않는다."""
    with self._lock:
        return sid in self._gui_burst

likelihood.reason: The agent must land its single in-flight GUI input in the handback's lock-held section: at ~5-10 ms per call in a tight loop and a few ms of audit write plus release, the collision is reachable within a session, and it needs no agent control over when the human hands back. Not certain per attempt, so not high.

impact.reason: The inputs themselves are still audited as tool_request/tool_result (coordinates, typed text), but their /workspace effects get no gui_changes diff and no snapshot is taken, so the burst-level attribution and recovery point the N-1 mitigation relies on silently misses an attacker-chosen window; the last snapshot predates the human takeover.

confidence.reason: Every trace line was re-checked in the 9805d91 tree and the minimum result was reproduced on the real AgentBox, GuiBursts and DesktopControl objects, with a control run showing the same inputs are recorded when a burst is open. The residual uncertainty is only how often the natural window is hit.
